html:
The second king of Rome in Roman tradition, said to have reigned from 715 to 673 BCE after Romulus. He was a Sabine, chosen for his wisdom and piety. Whether he lived is uncertain; the stories were written down centuries later by Livy and Plutarch.

Where Romulus was a warrior, Numa was remembered as the founder of Roman religion. Romans credited him with:

  • the priesthoods, including the pontifices, the flamens and the Vestal Virgins who kept the sacred fire
  • the calendar of festivals, and the addition of January and February to the year
  • the Temple of Janus, whose doors were closed in peace; they stayed shut through his whole reign

Legend said he was advised by the nymph Egeria. Later Romans looked back on him as the model of a peaceful, law-giving king, the opposite of the proud Tarquin whose fall led to the Roman Republic.
